questions.question: In a Linux shell, what does cd ~ do?
options: Changes to the current user's home directory
Changes to the filesystem root directory
Deletes temporary files from /tmp
Opens the last directory visited by another user
questions.explanation: The shell expands ~ to the current user's home directory. It is not the same as /, the filesystem root.

questions.question: A script exists at ./train.sh but running ./train.sh says Permission denied. Which command adds the missing execute bit?
options: chown root train.sh
chmod u+x train.sh
apt install train.sh
mv train.sh /usr/bin/
questions.explanation: chmod changes permission bits and u+x grants the owner execute permission. Ownership and moving the file are separate operations.

questions.question: What does sudo apt update do before a package installation?
options: Installs every package listed in the repository
Upgrades the NVIDIA driver without asking
Refresh package metadata
Changes the owner of the home directory
questions.explanation: apt update refreshes package metadata; apt install then uses that metadata to select and download a named package. The commands have different effects.

questions.question: Which command finds the largest immediate directories under / on a GNU/Linux GPU box?
options: free -h | grep /
cat /proc/meminfo | head -20
ls -la / | chmod +x
du, sort, and head
questions.explanation: du measures disk usage, sort -hr orders human-readable sizes numerically in reverse, and head limits the report. free and /proc/meminfo describe memory instead.

questions.question: Why does an in-place sed command often need different spelling on macOS and Linux?
options: BSD sed needs a -i suffix; GNU sed usually does not
Linux sed cannot use regular expressions
macOS sed can edit only files owned by root
The two systems use different newline characters for every text file
questions.explanation: The BSD and GNU sed interfaces differ around the -i argument. A portable script should choose the appropriate form or make its backup behavior explicit.

questions.question: A remote setup script fails with Permission denied while writing /opt/lesson. What is the responsible diagnosis?
options: Run sudo on every command until the error disappears
Inspect ownership and use narrow sudo
Delete /opt so the next command can recreate it
Change the file extension from .sh to .py
questions.explanation: The directory mode and ownership determine whether the user can write there. Inspecting them first avoids broad privilege use and preserves the machine's existing files.
